title: 01 · Your first waveform
summary: Run a small RC low-pass circuit, then inspect voltage and time with markers.
expected: The output rises smoothly after the input edge. No external PDK or simulator is needed.
steps: Open a copy, then press F5 to run the saved transient analysis.
Open Results → Waveforms and select the output trace.
Place X/Y markers and inspect their readings. Save your copy with Ctrl+S.

title: 02 · Native divider and studies
summary: An independent native circuit with a 1 V supply and two 1 kΩ resistors.
expected: The operating-point output is 0.5 V. ngspice is required; no external PDK is needed.
steps: Press F5 for the saved operating-point analysis.
Open Analysis → Variation cases to explore parameter studies.
Use R1.native.value as the resistor target. Compare results against the saved Output specification.

title: 03 · Inverter and linked layout
summary: Explore a small CMOS inverter in the schematic and layout views together.
expected: The output switches in the opposite direction to the input. Geometry and device models are educational.
steps: Select a device to inspect its electrical parameters and physical links.
Press F5 to run the saved transient analysis.
Use Verify → Geometry DRC (generic rules). These teaching rules do not represent a foundry process.

title: 04 · Layout parasitics
summary: Compare an RC circuit before and after adding declared interconnect resistance and capacitance.
expected: A short transient provides a baseline for the RC comparison. Coefficients are illustrative, not process-calibrated.
steps: Press F5 to run the baseline transient analysis.
Inspect the linked resistor and capacitor geometry.
Open Analysis → Post-layout → Distributed RC and specification comparison. Compare against the baseline waveform.

title: 05 · Reusable hierarchical cells
summary: Learn to instantiate a reusable divider and navigate between parent and child cells.
expected: The operating-point run evaluates the child circuit through its parent instance.
steps: Select the divider instance and enter its schematic.
Inspect the child ports, then return to the parent cell.
Run the saved operating-point analysis and save an independent copy.

title: 06 · Matching and placement
summary: Work with four resistors and saved common-centroid placement constraints.
expected: This is a placement exercise. Open the constraints and generate or adjust the matching layout.
steps: Inspect the resistor group and its saved placement constraints.
Open Layout → Placement and constraints to review the arrangement.
Generate placement, inspect device links and use Undo to compare alternatives.

title: 07 · GF180 bandgap startup
summary: Run the supplied bandgap at 5 V and 25 °C with the bundled GF180 transistor, bipolar and resistor models.
expected: One 3 ms startup transient. Inspect vref and avdd; this quick check is not full circuit qualification.
steps: Open a copy and press F5. NGSpice and the models are included in desktop packages.
Open Simulate → Program analyses for the waveform and measured final voltages.
Save your copy. The full original characterization is the next example.

title: 08 · GF180 full characterization
summary: The unchanged supplied 5vfullv2 schematic and its complete characterization program.
expected: 144 analyses, including startup, temperature, supply, load and AC tests. Allow several minutes or longer.
steps: Run the short startup example first to check installation.
Press F5 to run all 144 analyses. Inspect warnings and measurements as well as waveforms.
Use Open output files in Program analyses for the tables; /foss output paths are relocated to the run folder.

title: 09 · SKY130 transistor inverter
summary: A 1.8 V CMOS inverter using the included SKY130 transistor models.
expected: The output switches opposite to the input over a 12 ns transient.
steps: Open a copy and press F5. Models and symbols resolve automatically.
Inspect in and out under Simulate → Program analyses.
Choose Tools → Set up an open PDK → Use included PDKs to start your own native SKY130 project.
